subject: SLA tempo adjustment + negotiated burst credits for nightly batch windows
messages:
From: Priya Agarwal <ops@epochai.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Marco Rinaldi <marco@epochai.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: nightly batch tempo + temporary burst credits

Hi Vanessa,

Quick background: over the last 3 months our nightly analytics pipeline has grown from 200k to ~1.2M tokens per run (long-form summarization + reranking). The work is latency-insensitive (jobs complete in the midnight-to-6am window) but we need predictable completion times because downstream jobs assume availability by 07:30 PT.

We want to avoid downtime or long tail latency during those windows. Current Dedicated pool behavior causes some jobs to queue or be preempted during upstream daily traffic spikes. Can Redwood propose a temporary SLA amendment that: (a) guarantees a minimum effective throughput (tokens/sec equivalent) for EpochAI between 00:00–06:00 PT, and (b) provides a small pool of "burst credits" we can draw on for 30–60 minute spikes?

Attached is our nightly job profile and rough token distribution. We'd like a proposal and rough pricing impact to present to procurement next week.

Thanks,
Priya
Ops Lead, EpochAI

Attachments: epochai_nightly_profile_20261122.csv (attachment stub)
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: Priya Agarwal <ops@epochai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Request: nightly batch tempo + temporary burst credits

Priya —

Thanks for the clear profile and the ask. We can support a time-bounded throughput guarantee plus a burst credit pool; I'd like to propose an internal quick design before we produce formal language. Ben: can you draft an amendment template (throughput floor + burst credit accounting) and include telemetry/SLI changes we need? Lauren: we'll need a pricing delta and procurement language for the reserved pool amendment. Karthik: please flag any routing/fallback implications to Dedicated pools (preemption, sticky reservations).

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with your ops + ours tomorrow if that works.

— Vanessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, Priya Agarwal <ops@epochai.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: nightly batch tempo + temporary burst credits

Priya / team —

Summary of a practical amendment we can offer (initial proposal):

- Night window guarantee: allocate an effective throughput floor equivalent to 3 dedicated A100-equivalent slots (approx 120k tokens/sec sustained aggregated across your pool) between 00:00–06:00 PT, Monday–Sunday, for an initial 90-day term.
- Burst credits: grant an on-demand credit pool equal to 18 node-minutes per night (usable in contiguous or split bursts). Credits are consumed from the pool when your instantaneous demand exceeds the guaranteed floor. Unused credits do not roll over.
- Queueing behavior: during the guaranteed window, your queued requests will be served with priority ranking against other non-guaranteed workloads. Preemption will be limited; we will only evict workloads outside the guarantee unless an extreme capacity emergency is declared.
- Telemetry & enforcement: we will add an SLI (successful tokens served within window vs requested) and expose a per-night utilization report in Redwood Console; we'll also emit an event when burst credits dip below 25%.
- Pricing: incremental monthly charge for the 90-day pilot = base reserved pool + $X/day for burst credits (see attached spreadsheet for modeled scenarios).

Next steps: I attached a draft "tempo amendment" doc and a simple batch capacity CSV with modeling. Vanessa — if we agree to this draft, legal/procurement can review and we'll attach as an addendum to the existing Dedicated commitment.

Ben
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-tempo-amendment-epochai-v1.docx (attachment stub); burst_pricing_model.csv (attachment stub)
From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, Priya Agarwal <ops@epochai.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: nightly batch tempo + temporary burst credits

Thanks Ben — very clear. A couple quick legal/procurement clarifications we need before we push to DocuSign: 

1) Term & termination: confirm that the 90-day pilot can be terminated with 15 days notice by either party for operational reasons; otherwise it becomes a standard addendum rolled into the annual commitment.
2) Metrics & credits: define exact token accounting (e.g., how we convert model inference units to "tokens served" for multi-model pipelines). We should include a worked example in the amendment.
3) SLAs & remedies: if we miss the guaranteed floor more than X nights in a 30-day window, credits to the customer should be defined (we typically provide pro-rated token credits).

Priya — can you confirm your tolerance for a 15-day pilot termination clause and whether you prefer token credits or service credits in the remedy? Also, please supply a sample job that represents your 95th-percentile nightly run (we can use that to finalize the token accounting example).

— Lauren
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Agarwal <ops@epochai.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: nightly batch tempo + temporary burst credits

Lauren / Ben / Vanessa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft. We can accept a 90-day pilot with 15 days' termination notice. For remedies, EpochAI prefers token credits (easier for our billing reconciliation). I've attached a representative job manifest (95th-percentile run) and timezone details; the job runs at ~02:10 PT and takes ~18–24 minutes when fully provisioned.

If you can add a short worked example showing how a 24-minute spike centered at 02:10 consumes burst credits and what the customer would see in the Console billing view, we're ready to move to legal review. Also please share an estimate for the incremental monthly cost so procurement can greenlight a DocuSign route.

Thanks — Priya
Ops Lead, EpochAI
